A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Rate-In. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v3 reports original synthetic-regression, medical-image classification, segmentation, sensitivity, and runtime results in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original results and adds MedMNIST-C corruption experiments and an ImageNet information-loss analysis.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same sequential, per-layer and per-input dropout adjustment using information-loss feedback. The MI implementation and SSIM alternative already appear in v3; the additional evaluated architectures do not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: v4 adds corrupted PathMNIST-C, BloodMNIST-C, and TissueMNIST-C inputs, extending evaluation to modality-specific imaging artifacts and severity levels. Appendix B also adds ImageNet natural images for layer-sensitivity analysis. The original synthetic and medical tasks remain.

E2.justification: The peripheral-zone comparator in Table 2 switches from activation-based dropout in v3 to constant dropout in v4, as verified against their detailed appendix tables. The complete Constant, Scheduled, and Activation comparator suite remains unchanged, including its extension to corrupted inputs.

E3.justification: The added corruption evaluation aggregates performance across corruption types and severity levels. The new ImageNet analysis uses MobileNet-V3-Large, VGG-16, and ResNet-50 with dropout after every convolutional layer. Settings for the retained experiments, including 30 MC passes and optimization limits, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds systematic medical-image corruption robustness tests in Section 4.3 and Table 5, plus cross-architecture information-loss sensitivity analysis on ImageNet in Figure 12. The existing noise, training-size, convergence, runtime, and MI-versus-SSIM analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose the same synthetic-experiment random seed and retain the same timing means, standard deviations, and worst-case reporting. v4 introduces no additional repeated-run counts, confidence-interval procedures, or significance tests for comparative performance.

E6.justification: v4 adds extensive corruption results and ImageNet layer-loss findings. For example, Table 5 reports TissueMNIST-C ACC/AUARC of 0.45/0.48 for Rate-In versus 0.12/0.07 for Scheduled dropout at p, epsilon = 0.20. Existing same-method results are retained; Table 2's changed peripheral benchmark values reflect comparator substitution.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, information-loss formulations, and computational-complexity derivation are retained. v4's main-text complexity subsection summarizes analysis already present in v3 Appendix B; it adds no theorem, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims: label-free inference-time adaptation of dropout by layer and input, improving uncertainty estimation while preserving predictive performance. The additional experiments support this retained contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly interprets the corruption results as broad OOD stability, including superiority across all corruption types. This generalization exceeds Table 5, which contains exceptions such as PathMNIST-C JPEG corruption at p, epsilon = 0.20. Existing mechanism explanations, convergence failures, and Appendix C limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly specifies the ImageNet study's PyTorch architectures, IMAGENET1K_V1 pretrained weights, and dropout placement. v4 also identifies the corruption protocol source and explains benchmark selection in Table 4. Existing training details, hardware, software versions, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2 substantially broaden positioning through explicit comparisons with post-hoc dropout injection and infer-dropout, alongside coverage of test-time augmentation, noise injection, MC batch/layer normalization, and Masksembles. v4 also adds benchmark and software references and removes the Segment Anything in Medical Images reference.

P1.justification: v4 tightens prose, nests classification and segmentation under Results, adds appendix navigation, and brings an existing complexity summary into the main text. The principal narrative, algorithm exposition, and discussion structure remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v4 changes the document template and table formatting, including row order, joint p/epsilon headers, and benchmark markings. It adds two corruption tables and the ImageNet figure, and relocates v3 Figure 4 to Appendix B as Figure 11. Existing graphical content is retained.

improvement.justification: The new corruption tests provide direct evidence for an important previously untested aspect of Rate-In's claimed adaptability, while the ImageNet analysis and clearer benchmark selection improve assessment of applicability. However, Section 4.3 overstates superiority across all corruption types: Table 5 includes counterexamples, including PathMNIST-C JPEG corruption. The added evidence provides a net benefit, but this overgeneralization limits the quality gain.
